title: IIT JAM 2027 Chemistry (CY) — Full Length Mock Test 10
titleEn: IIT JAM 2027 Chemistry (CY) — Full Length Mock Test 10

questions.questionTextEn: Catalytic hydrogenation of hex-3-yne using $\text{H}_2$ over Lindlar's catalyst ($\text{Pd/CaCO}_3$ poisoned with $\text{Pb(OAc)}_2$ and quinoline) yields predominantly
questions.explanationEn: Lindlar's catalyst is a poisoned palladium catalyst that selectively stops hydrogenation of an internal alkyne at the alkene stage via **syn-addition** of $\text{H}_2$ on the catalyst surface, giving the *cis* alkene, **$(Z)$-hex-3-ene**. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: For an enzyme-catalyzed reaction following Michaelis–Menten kinetics, the substrate concentration $[S]$ at which the initial reaction rate $v_0$ equals $\frac{1}{4}V_{\max}$ is
questions.explanationEn: From $v_0 = \frac{V_{\max}[S]}{K_M + [S]} = \frac{1}{4}V_{\max}$, we get $4[S] = K_M + [S] \implies 3[S] = K_M \implies [S] = K_M/3$.

questions.questionTextEn: According to Hückel's rule, the cyclopropenyl cation ($\text{C}_3\text{H}_3^+$) is classified as
questions.explanationEn: The cyclopropenyl cation is cyclic, planar, fully conjugated, and possesses $2\pi$ electrons, satisfying $(4n + 2)$ with $n = 0$; hence it is aromatic.

questions.questionTextEn: Azulene (bicyclo[5.3.0]decapentaene) exhibits a remarkably large permanent dipole moment ($\mu \approx 1.08\text{ D}$) for a hydrocarbon because its major dipolar resonance contributor places
optionsEn: positive charge on the five-membered ring and negative charge on the seven-membered ring
negative charge on the five-membered ring and positive charge on the seven-membered ring
negative charge equally on all ten carbons
both charges localized on the shared ring-junction bond
questions.explanationEn: Charge separation in azulene generates a fused cyclopentadienyl anion ($6\pi$, aromatic) and tropylium cation ($6\pi$, aromatic), placing negative charge on the 5-membered ring and positive charge on the 7-membered ring.

questions.questionTextEn: Among the halogens $\text{F}$, $\text{Cl}$, $\text{Br}$, and $\text{I}$, the element with the most negative first electron gain enthalpy (highest electron affinity) is
questions.explanationEn: Although fluorine is the most electronegative element, its $2p$ subshell is very compact, leading to strong interelectronic repulsion when an extra electron is added. Chlorine adds the electron to a more diffuse $3p$ subshell with less repulsion, giving $\text{Cl}$ the most negative electron gain enthalpy ($-349\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ vs. $-328\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ for $\text{F}$).

questions.questionTextEn: According to Taube's classification of octahedral $3d$ transition metal complexes, which one of the following pairs consists exclusively of **kinetically inert** complexes?
questions.explanationEn: Octahedral $d^3$ ($[\text{Cr(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$: $t_{2g}^3 e_g^0$) and low-spin $d^6$ ($[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$: $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$) complexes have empty antibonding $e_g$ orbitals and high ligand field activation energies (LFAE), making them classically kinetically inert toward ligand substitution.

questions.questionTextEn: According to the Clausius–Clapeyron equation for liquid–vapor equilibrium (assuming ideal vapor and $V_g \gg V_l$), a plot of $\ln P$ versus $\dfrac{1}{T}$ is a straight line with slope
questions.explanationEn: Integrating $\frac{d\ln P}{dT} = \frac{\Delta H_{\text{vap}}}{RT^2}$ gives $\ln P = -\frac{\Delta H_{\text{vap}}}{R}\left(\frac{1}{T}\right) + C$, so the slope of $\ln P$ vs. $1/T$ is $-\frac{\Delta H_{\text{vap}}}{R}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following octahedral complexes is optically active (chiral)?
questions.explanationEn: $\textit{cis}\text{-[Co(en)}_2\text{Cl}_2]^+$ belongs to the $C_2$ point group and lacks any mirror plane or inversion center, existing as a non-superimposable $\Delta$/$\Lambda$ enantiomeric pair. All other listed complexes possess at least one mirror plane ($\sigma$) and are achiral.

questions.questionTextEn: The decreasing order of aromaticity among the five-membered heterocycles thiophene, pyrrole, and furan is
questions.explanationEn: Aromaticity in 5-membered heterocycles depends on how readily the heteroatom donates its lone pair into the $6\,\pi$ sextet (inversely related to heteroatom electronegativity): sulfur ($\chi = 2.58$, thiophene, $\text{RE} \approx 121\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) $>$ nitrogen ($\chi = 3.04$, pyrrole, $\text{RE} \approx 88\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$) $>$ oxygen ($\chi = 3.44$, furan, $\text{RE} \approx 67\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$). Hence, option **(C)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: The value of the definite integral $\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1} \left(x^3 \cos x + x^2\right)\,dx$ is
questions.explanationEn: Since $x^3\cos x$ is an odd function, its integral over the symmetric interval $[-1, 1]$ is $0$. Since $x^2$ is even, $\int_{-1}^{1} x^2\,dx = 2\int_0^1 x^2\,dx = 2\left[\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_0^1 = \frac{2}{3}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which single chemical test cleanly distinguishes **pent-1-yne** from **pent-2-yne**?
optionsEn: Treatment with $\text{Br}_2/\text{CCl}_4$, which decolorizes only with pent-1-yne
Treatment with ammoniacal silver nitrate ($[\text{Ag(NH}_3)_2]^+$), which gives a white precipitate only with pent-1-yne
Treatment with cold dilute alkaline $\text{KMnO}_4$, which decolorizes only with pent-2-yne
Treatment with 2,4-DNP reagent, which gives an orange precipitate only with pent-1-yne
questions.explanationEn: Pent-1-yne is a terminal alkyne possessing an acidic $sp$-$	ext{C–H}$ proton and reacts with ammoniacal $\text{AgNO}_3$ (or ammoniacal $\text{CuCl}$) to precipitate silver acetylide ($\text{R–C}\equiv\text{C}^-\text{Ag}^+$), whereas internal pent-2-yne does not react.

questions.questionTextEn: In the **Hantzsch pyridine synthesis**, condensation of 2 equivalents of ethyl acetoacetate, 1 equivalent of benzaldehyde, and 1 equivalent of ammonia yields a 1,4-dihydropyridine intermediate, which upon oxidation with $\text{HNO}_3$ or DDQ affords
questions.explanationEn: The Hantzsch synthesis combines $2\text{ equiv}$ of $\beta$-keto ester (ethyl acetoacetate), $1\text{ equiv}$ of aldehyde (benzaldehyde, supplying C4 and its substituent), and $1\text{ equiv}$ of $\text{NH}_3$ (supplying N1) to form symmetrical diethyl 2,6-dimethyl-4-phenyl-1,4-dihydropyridine-3,5-dicarboxylate, which oxidizes to **diethyl 2,6-dimethyl-4-phenylpyridine-3,5-dicarboxylate**. Hence, option **(A)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: The correct increasing order of $\text{O}-\text{O}$ bond length among the dioxygen species $\text{O}_2^+$, $\text{O}_2$, $\text{O}_2^-$, and $\text{O}_2^{2-}$ is
questions.explanationEn: The MOT bond orders are: $\text{O}_2^+$ ($2.5$), $\text{O}_2$ ($2.0$), $\text{O}_2^-$ ($1.5$), and $\text{O}_2^{2-}$ ($1.0$). Since bond length is inversely related to bond order, the increasing order of $\text{O}-\text{O}$ bond length is $\text{O}_2^+ < \text{O}_2 < \text{O}_2^- < \text{O}_2^{2-}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Free iron(II) porphyrins bind $\text{CO}$ roughly $20{,}000$ times more strongly than $\text{O}_2$, whereas in myoglobin and hemoglobin this preference is reduced to roughly $200\text{--}250$ times. The key structural feature of the globin pocket responsible for this discrimination is
optionsEn: the proximal histidine directly blocking $\text{CO}$ coordination
the distal histidine (His E7), which forms a stabilizing hydrogen bond to bent bound $\text{O}_2$ and sterically hinders the preferred linear $\text{Fe}-\text{C}-\text{O}$ geometry
oxidation of $\text{CO}$ to $\text{CO}_2$ by the heme iron
conversion of heme to a chlorin ring upon $\text{CO}$ binding
questions.explanationEn: Bound $\text{O}_2$ naturally adopts a bent geometry ($\angle\text{Fe}-\text{O}-\text{O} \approx 115^\circ\text{--}120^\circ$) and accepts a strong hydrogen bond from the distal histidine (His E7). Conversely, $\text{CO}$ prefers a linear geometry perpendicular to the heme plane, which is sterically clashed by the distal pocket (and $\text{CO}$ is a much poorer H-bond acceptor).

questions.questionTextEn: Unlike $n$-butane, 1,2-difluoroethane ($\text{FCH}_2\text{–CH}_2\text{F}$) is **more stable** in its *gauche* conformation than in its *anti* conformation in the gas phase. This preference (the *gauche* effect) is best explained by
optionsEn: minimization of the molecular dipole moment in the *gauche* conformer.
steric repulsion between the two hydrogens in the *anti* conformer.
hyperconjugative donation from the electron-rich $\sigma_{\text{C–H}}$ bonding orbital into the low-lying antiperiplanar $\sigma^*_{\text{C–F}}$ antibonding orbital.
questions.explanationEn: In the *gauche* conformation of $\text{FCH}_2\text{–CH}_2\text{F}$, each $\text{C–H}$ bond (a better $\sigma$-donor than $\text{C–F}$) is aligned antiperiplanar ($180^\circ$) to a strongly accepting $\sigma^*_{\text{C–F}}$ orbital, maximizing stabilizing $\sigma_{\text{C–H}} \to \sigma^*_{\text{C–F}}$ hyperconjugation.

questions.questionTextEn: Birch reduction of benzoic acid ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CO}_2\text{H}$) using $\text{Na}$ in liquid $\text{NH}_3$ and ethanol followed by acidification yields
questions.explanationEn: An electron-withdrawing group ($-\text{CO}_2^-$ in liquid $\text{NH}_3$) stabilizes negative charge at the ***ipso* and *para* carbons** in the Birch radical anion/carbanion intermediates. Protonation therefore occurs at C1 (*ipso*) and C4 (*para*), placing the remaining two double bonds at $\text{C2}=\text{C3}$ and $\text{C5}=\text{C6}$ to yield **cyclohexa-2,5-diene-1-carboxylic acid**. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In the **Skraup synthesis** of quinoline from aniline, glycerol, concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, and nitrobenzene, the role of nitrobenzene is to act as
optionsEn: a mild oxidizing agent that dehydrogenates dihydroquinoline to aromatic quinoline
questions.explanationEn: In the Skraup synthesis, conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ dehydrates glycerol to acrolein, which undergoes Michael addition with aniline and acid-catalyzed cyclization to form **1,2-dihydroquinoline**. **Nitrobenzene** acts as the **oxidizing agent** (aromatizing 1,2-dihydroquinoline to quinoline while being reduced to aniline). Hence, option **(C)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Treatment of 3-methoxybromobenzene (*m*-bromoanisole) with $\text{NaNH}_2$ in liquid $\text{NH}_3$ yields predominantly
questions.explanationEn: In 3-methoxybromobenzene, the inductive $-I$ effect of the $-\text{OMe}$ group makes the C2 proton (between $-\text{OMe}$ and $-\text{Br}$) the most acidic, so elimination gives **3-methoxybenzyne** (triple bond at C2–C3 relative to OMe at C1). Subsequent addition of $\text{NH}_2^-$ occurs selectively at **C3** (the *meta* carbon) so that the developing negative charge is placed at **C2** (*ortho* to the $-I$ $-\text{OMe}$ group, where it is inductively stabilized). Protonation yields **3-methoxyaniline (*m*-anisidine)** predominantly. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: In Taube's classic redox reaction between $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]^{2+}$ and $[\text{Cr(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$ in acidic aqueous solution, the immediate chromium-containing product isolated is $[\text{Cr(H}_2\text{O)}_5\text{Cl}]^{2+}$. This observation provides direct proof of
optionsEn: an outer-sphere electron transfer mechanism with no ligand bridging
an inner-sphere electron transfer mechanism proceeding through a chloro-bridged $[(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Co}-\text{Cl}-\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5]^{4+}$ intermediate
rapid substitution of $\text{Cl}^-$ into kinetically inert $[\text{Cr(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$ after electron transfer
homolytic cleavage of the $\text{Co}-\text{Cl}$ bond prior to collision
questions.explanationEn: Because $[\text{Cr(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$ ($d^3$) is kinetically inert, it cannot rapidly pick up free $\text{Cl}^-$ from solution after electron transfer. Isolating $[\text{Cr(H}_2\text{O)}_5\text{Cl}]^{2+}$ proves that $\text{Cl}^-$ bridged the labile $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ and inert $\text{Co}^{3+}$ centers during electron transfer, followed by cleavage of the weakened $\text{Co}^{2+}-\text{Cl}$ bond.

questions.questionTextEn: The thermal Diels–Alder reaction of cyclopentadiene with maleic anhydride yields predominantly the *endo* adduct rather than the thermodynamically more stable *exo* adduct because
optionsEn: the *endo* transition state has less steric crowding
secondary orbital interactions between the carbonyl $\pi^*$ orbitals of maleic anhydride and the diene $\pi$ HOMO lower the *endo* activation barrier
maleic anhydride reacts only via a stepwise zwitterionic pathway
the *exo* pathway is symmetry-forbidden by Woodward–Hoffmann rules
questions.explanationEn: Both *endo* and *exo* $[4+2]$ cycloadditions are symmetry-allowed. Under kinetic control, the ***endo* transition state** is stabilized by favorable **secondary orbital interactions** between the $\pi^*$ orbitals of the anhydride carbonyls and the developing $\text{C2}=\text{C3}$ $\pi$-orbital of cyclopentadiene, lowering its activation energy relative to the *exo* pathway. Hence, option **(B)** is correct.

questions.questionTextEn: For a binary mixture of components $1$ and $2$ at constant temperature and pressure, the Gibbs–Duhem equation states that
questions.explanationEn: At constant $T$ and $P$, the Gibbs–Duhem equation is $\sum_i n_i\,d\mu_i = 0$. Dividing by total moles $n = n_1 + n_2$ yields $x_1\,d\mu_1 + x_2\,d\mu_2 = 0$.

questions.questionTextEn: When $[\text{CH}_3\text{Mn(CO)}_5]$ is treated with isotopically labeled $^{13}\text{CO}$ to form $[(\text{CH}_3\text{CO})\text{Mn(CO)}_4(^{13}\text{CO})]$, spectroscopic analysis proves that
optionsEn: the incoming $^{13}\text{CO}$ inserts directly into the $\text{Mn}-\text{CH}_3$ bond to form a $-\text{C}(=\text{O})\text{CH}_3$ group containing $^{13}\text{C}$
the methyl group migrates onto an existing *cis*-coordinated $^{12}\text{CO}$ ligand, and the incoming $^{13}\text{CO}$ occupies the vacant coordination site exclusively *cis* to the acetyl group
the incoming $^{13}\text{CO}$ occupies the site exclusively *trans* to the acetyl group
the reaction proceeds via a free methyl radical
questions.explanationEn: In Calderazzo's classic $^{13}\text{CO}$ labeling experiment on $[\text{CH}_3\text{Mn(CO)}_5]$, no $^{13}\text{C}$ appears in the acetyl carbonyl, and the incoming $^{13}\text{CO}$ is found exclusively *cis* to the acetyl ligand, proving **methyl migration** onto an adjacent *cis*-$\text{CO}$ followed by coordination of $^{13}\text{CO}$ at the vacated *cis* site.

questions.questionTextEn: An ester hydrolysis reaction is studied in acetic acid/sodium acetate buffers at constant $\text{pH} = 4.76$ while the total buffer concentration ($[\text{HA}] + [\text{A}^-]$) is tripled at constant ionic strength. If the observed pseudo-first-order rate constant $k_{\text{obs}}$ remains completely unchanged, the reaction exhibits
questions.explanationEn: In **specific acid/base catalysis**, the rate depends solely on $[\text{H}_3\text{O}^+]$ and/or $[\text{OH}^-]$ (i.e., on $\text{pH}$ alone) and is independent of the concentration of undissociated buffer acid $\text{HA}$ or conjugate base $\text{A}^-$ at fixed $\text{pH}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which one of the following pairs of transition metals exhibits nearly identical atomic and ionic radii primarily as a consequence of lanthanoid contraction?
questions.explanationEn: Between the $4d$ element $\text{Zr}$ ($Z=40$) and the $5d$ element $\text{Hf}$ ($Z=72$), $14$ lanthanoid elements intervene in which electrons enter the poorly shielding $4f$ subshell. The resulting increase in $Z_{\text{eff}}$ contracts the $5d$ orbitals so that $\text{Zr}$ ($r_{\text{cov}} \approx 145\text{ pm}$) and $\text{Hf}$ ($r_{\text{cov}} \approx 144\text{ pm}$) have nearly identical sizes and very similar chemistry.

questions.questionTextEn: A conductivity cell filled with $0.02\text{ M}$ $\text{KCl}$ ($\kappa = 2.768 \times 10^{-3}\text{ S cm}^{-1}$) has a resistance of $100\ \Omega$ at $298\text{ K}$. When filled with a $0.01\text{ M}$ solution of electrolyte $MX$, its resistance is $553.6\ \Omega$. The molar conductivity $\Lambda_m$ of the $0.01\text{ M}$ $MX$ solution is
questions.explanationEn: Cell constant $G^* = \kappa_{\text{KCl}} \times R_{\text{KCl}} = 2.768 \times 10^{-3} \times 100 = 0.2768\text{ cm}^{-1}$. For $MX$, $\kappa_{MX} = G^* / R_{MX} = 0.2768 / 553.6 = 5.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ S cm}^{-1}$. Hence $\Lambda_m = \frac{1000\,\kappa_{MX}}{c} = \frac{1000 \times 5.0 \times 10^{-4}}{0.01} = 50.0\text{ S cm}^2\text{ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn:
An organic compound $\text{C}_8\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$ exhibits IR absorption at $1725\text{ cm}^{-1}$ (no broad band above $3100\text{ cm}^{-1}$) and the following $^1\text{H}$ NMR spectrum:
$\delta\ 7.35\text{ (m, 5H)}$, $5.12\text{ (s, 2H)}$, $2.08\text{ (s, 3H)}$
The structure of the compound is
questions.explanationEn: The $5\text{H}$ multiplet at $\delta\ 7.35$ indicates a monosubstituted phenyl ring (ruling out 4-methylbenzoic acid). The absence of a triplet–quartet rules out ethyl benzoate. The $2\text{H}$ singlet at $\delta\ 5.12$ is strongly deshielded by both phenyl and ester oxygen ($\text{PhCH}_2\text{O–}$), whereas in methyl 2-phenylacetate the benzylic $\text{CH}_2$ would appear near $\delta\ 3.6$ and the $\text{OCH}_3$ near $\delta\ 3.7$. Thus the compound is benzyl acetate.

questions.questionTextEn: In an Ostwald viscometer at $25\,^\circ\text{C}$, equal volumes of water ($\rho = 1.00\text{ g cm}^{-3}$, $\eta = 1.00\text{ cP}$) and an organic liquid ($\rho = 0.80\text{ g cm}^{-3}$) take $50\text{ s}$ and $75\text{ s}$, respectively, to flow between the two marks. The viscosity of the organic liquid is
questions.explanationEn: Using the Ostwald viscometer relation $\frac{\eta_2}{\eta_1} = \frac{\rho_2 t_2}{\rho_1 t_1}$, we get $\eta_2 = 1.00 \times \frac{0.80 \times 75}{1.00 \times 50} = 1.20\text{ cP}$.

questions.questionTextEn: For a rigid diatomic rotor with rotational constant $B$ (in $\text{cm}^{-1}$) at absolute temperature $T$, the rotational quantum number $J_{\max}$ corresponding to the maximum thermal population is given by
questions.explanationEn: The population of rotational level $J$ is proportional to $(2J + 1)\exp\left[-\frac{hcB J(J+1)}{k_B T}\right]$. Setting $\frac{dN_J}{dJ} = 0$ yields $2 - (2J+1)^2\frac{hcB}{k_B T} = 0 \implies 2J + 1 = \sqrt{\frac{2k_B T}{hcB}} \implies J_{\max} = \sqrt{\frac{k_B T}{2hcB}} - \frac{1}{2}$.

questions.questionTextEn: When $1000\text{ J}$ of heat is transferred irreversibly from a large thermal reservoir at $500\text{ K}$ to another large thermal reservoir at $250\text{ K}$, the total entropy change of the universe ($\Delta S_{\text{univ}}$) is
questions.explanationEn: The total entropy change is $\Delta S_{\text{univ}} = \Delta S_{\text{hot}} + \Delta S_{\text{cold}} = \frac{-1000}{500} + \frac{+1000}{250} = -2.0 + 4.0 = +2.0\text{ J K}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: For the hydrogen atom emission spectrum, the ratio of the shortest wavelength of the Balmer series to the longest wavelength of the Lyman series is
questions.explanationEn: The shortest wavelength (series limit) of the Balmer series ($n = \infty \to 2$) has $\frac{1}{\lambda_{B,\min}} = R_H\left(\frac{1}{2^2} - 0\right) = \frac{R_H}{4} \implies \lambda_{B,\min} = \frac{4}{R_H}$. The longest wavelength of the Lyman series ($n = 2 \to 1$) has $\frac{1}{\lambda_{L,\max}} = R_H\left(1 - \frac{1}{4}\right) = \frac{3R_H}{4} \implies \lambda_{L,\max} = \frac{4}{3R_H}$. Their ratio is $\frac{4/R_H}{4/(3R_H)} = 3$.

questions.questionTextEn: For a first-order reaction $A \to P$ with rate constant $k$, the correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: The half-life $t_{1/2}$ is independent of the initial concentration $[A]_0$.
The fraction of reactant remaining after $m$ half-lives is $(1/2)^m$.
A plot of $\ln[A]_t$ versus $t$ is a straight line with slope $-k$.
The time required for $90\%$ completion is twice the time required for $50\%$ completion.
questions.explanationEn: (A), (B), and (C) are standard properties of first-order kinetics ($[A]_t = [A]_0 e^{-kt}$, $t_{1/2} = \ln 2 / k$). (D) is false because $t_{90\%}/t_{50\%} = \frac{\ln 10}{\ln 2} \approx 3.32$, not $2$.

questions.questionTextEn: For a diprotic weak acid $\text{H}_2\text{A}$ with well-separated dissociation constants ($K_{a1} \gg K_{a2}$), the correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: In a pure aqueous solution of $\text{H}_2\text{A}$ (not extremely dilute), $[\text{A}^{2-}] \approx K_{a2}$.
The $\text{pH}$ of an aqueous solution of the amphiprotic salt $\text{NaHA}$ is approximately $\dfrac{\text{p}K_{a1} + \text{p}K_{a2}}{2}$.
At $\text{pH} = \text{p}K_{a1}$, the concentrations $[\text{H}_2\text{A}]$ and $[\text{HA}^-]$ are equal.
For any diprotic acid, $K_{a2}$ is always greater than $K_{a1}$.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) True:** From the first dissociation, $[\text{H}^+] \approx [\text{HA}^-]$, so $K_{a2} = \frac{[\text{H}^+][\text{A}^{2-}]}{[\text{HA}^-]} \implies [\text{A}^{2-}] \approx K_{a2}$.
- **(B) True:** Standard amphiprotic salt approximation.
- **(C) True:** By Henderson–Hasselbalch, $\text{pH} = \text{p}K_{a1}$ when $[\text{HA}^-] = [\text{H}_2\text{A}]$.
- **(D) False:** Removing a proton from an anionic $\text{HA}^-$ is harder than from neutral $\text{H}_2\text{A}$, so $K_{a1} > K_{a2}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Let $A$ and $B$ be invertible $n \times n$ real matrices. Which of the following identity/identities ALWAYS hold(s)?
questions.explanationEn: All four are fundamental matrix identities: transpose and inverse reverse multiplication order, determinant is multiplicative ($\det(AB) = \det(A)\det(B)$), and trace is linear ($\text{Tr}(A+B) = \text{Tr}(A)+\text{Tr}(B)$).

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) regarding oxoacids of phosphorus is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_2$ and $\text{H}_3\text{PO}_3$ both act as reducing agents because they contain direct $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds.
Pyrophosphoric acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7$) contains one $\text{P}-\text{O}-\text{P}$ bridge and four $-\text{OH}$ groups.
Hypophosphoric acid ($\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_6$) contains a direct $\text{P}-\text{P}$ single bond.
In cyclic trimetaphosphoric acid ($\text{H}_3\text{P}_3\text{O}_9$), phosphorus is in the $+3$ oxidation state.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A) True: Direct $\text{P}-\text{H}$ bonds impart strong reducing character (e.g., reducing $\text{Ag}^+$ to $\text{Ag}$).
- (B) True: $\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_7$ is $(\text{HO})_2\text{P}(=\text{O})-\text{O}-\text{P}(=\text{O})(\text{OH})_2$.
- (C) True: $\text{H}_4\text{P}_2\text{O}_6$ is $(\text{HO})_2\text{P}(=\text{O})-\text{P}(=\text{O})(\text{OH})_2$ with a $\text{P}-\text{P}$ bond ($\text{P}$ is $+4$).
- (D) False: In $(\text{HPO}_3)_3$, phosphorus is in the $+5$ oxidation state.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about the **Birch reduction** ($\text{Na/liq. NH}_3$, $\text{EtOH}$) of substituted benzenes is/are correct?
optionsEn: Electron-donating groups (such as $-\text{OMe}$ or $-\text{CH}_3$) remain attached to a double-bond ($sp^2$) carbon in the 1,4-cyclohexadiene product.
Electron-withdrawing groups (such as $-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$) end up attached to a saturated ($sp^3$) carbon in the 1,4-cyclohexadiene product.
Unconjugated 1,4-cyclohexadienes are formed under kinetic protonation of the pentadienyl carbanion at its central carbon.
Isolated disubstituted alkenes are rapidly reduced to alkanes under standard Birch conditions.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** EDGs destabilize *ipso* negative charge, leaving the *ipso* carbon unreduced ($sp^2$).
- **(B) Correct:** EWGs stabilize *ipso* negative charge, so *ipso* and *para* carbons are protonated ($sp^3$).
- **(C) Correct:** The symmetrical pentadienyl anion has its largest electron density at the central carbon (C3), so kinetic protonation gives the unconjugated 1,4-diene.
- **(D) Incorrect:** Isolated non-conjugated alkenes are inert to $\text{Na/liq. NH}_3$.
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following octahedral complexes is/are expected to undergo a **strong** Jahn–Teller distortion (due to unequal occupancy of the $e_g$ orbitals)?
questions.explanationEn:
Strong Jahn–Teller distortion occurs for unsymmetrically occupied $e_g$ sets:
- (A) High-spin $d^4$ ($t_{2g}^3 e_g^1$): strong distortion. True.
- (B) Low-spin $d^7$ ($t_{2g}^6 e_g^1$): strong distortion. True.
- (C) $d^9$ ($t_{2g}^6 e_g^3$): strong distortion. True.
- (D) Low-spin $d^6$ ($t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$): non-degenerate $^1A_{1g}$, no distortion. False.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statement(s) about the octahedral crystal field splitting parameter $\Delta_o$ is/are **CORRECT**?
optionsEn: For a given metal and ligands, $\Delta_o$ increases with increasing oxidation state of the metal ion (e.g., $[\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+} > [\text{Fe(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{2+}$).
Descending a transition metal triad for the same oxidation state and ligands, $\Delta_o$ increases in the order $3d < 4d < 5d$.
For $d^1, d^2, d^3, d^8,$ and $d^9$ octahedral complexes, only a single spin state is possible regardless of ligand field strength.
For a $d^5$ octahedral complex, both high-spin and low-spin states have zero CFSE.
questions.explanationEn:
- (A), (B), (C) are all fundamental CFT rules.
- (D) False: High-spin $d^5$ ($t_{2g}^3 e_g^2$) has $\text{CFSE} = 0$, whereas low-spin $d^5$ ($t_{2g}^5 e_g^0$) has $\text{CFSE} = -2.0\Delta_o + 2P \neq 0$.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following statements about DNA and RNA structure is/are correct?
optionsEn: In Watson–Crick double-stranded DNA, the molar ratio of adenine equals thymine ($\text{A} = \text{T}$) and guanine equals cytosine ($\text{G} = \text{C}$) (Chargaff's rules).
DNA with a higher $\text{G}+\text{C}$ content has a higher melting temperature ($T_m$) than DNA of equal length with higher $\text{A}+\text{T}$ content.
The two strands of a B-DNA double helix run in an antiparallel orientation ($5' \to 3'$ paired with $3' \to 5'$).
RNA contains thymine paired with adenine as its standard canonical base.
questions.explanationEn:
- **(A) Correct:** Chargaff's base-equivalence rules follow directly from $\text{A}=\text{T}$ and $\text{G}\equiv\text{C}$ pairing.
- **(B) Correct:** $\text{G}-\text{C}$ pairs have 3 hydrogen bonds (and stronger $\pi$-stacking) vs. 2 for $\text{A}-\text{T}$, raising $T_m$.
- **(C) Correct:** Double-stranded B-DNA is antiparallel.
- **(D) Incorrect:** RNA contains **uracil (U)** instead of thymine (T).
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following pairs of reactants will yield 3-methylpentan-3-ol after aqueous $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ workup?
questions.explanationEn:
The target alcohol is $\text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)(Et)}_2$ (3-methylpentan-3-ol):
- **(A) Correct:** $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{Et} + 2\,\text{EtMgBr} \to \text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)(Et)}_2$.
- **(B) Correct:** $\text{CH}_3\text{COEt} + \text{EtMgBr} \to \text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)(Et)}_2$.
- **(C) Correct:** $\text{Et}_2\text{CO} + \text{MeMgBr} \to \text{CH}_3\text{C(OH)(Et)}_2$.
- **(D) Incorrect:** $\text{EtCO}_2\text{Me} + 2\,\text{MeMgBr} \to \text{EtC(OH)(Me)}_2$ (2-methylbutan-2-ol).
Hence, **(A), (B), and (C)** are correct.

questions.questionTextEn: Regarding the conformational analysis of $n$-butane about the C2–C3 bond, the correct statement(s) is/are
optionsEn: The *anti* conformer (dihedral angle $180^\circ$) is the global energy minimum and belongs to the $C_{2h}$ point group.
The two *gauche* conformers ($+60^\circ$ and $-60^\circ$) are non-superimposable mirror images (conformational enantiomers) belonging to the $C_2$ point group.
The fully eclipsed (*syn*-periplanar, $0^\circ$) conformer has the highest energy due to both torsional strain and $\text{CH}_3\text{–CH}_3$ steric repulsion.
The *gauche* conformer is lower in energy than the *anti* conformer.
questions.explanationEn: (A), (B), and (C) are correct. In $n$-butane, the *gauche* conformer is $\sim 3.8\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ **higher** in energy than the *anti* conformer, so (D) is false.

questions.questionTextEn:
The molecular weight of **thiophene** ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_4\text{S}$) is _______ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$. *(answer in integer)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{S} = 32$]
questions.explanationEn: Thiophene ($\text{C}_4\text{H}_4\text{S}$) has molecular weight $= 4(12) + 4(1) + 32 = \mathbf{84}\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn:
The molecular weight of the major *ortho*-formylated product obtained in the Reimer–Tiemann reaction of phenol with $\text{CHCl}_3/\text{aq. NaOH}$ (after acidification) is _______ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$. *(answer in integer)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{O} = 16$]
questions.explanationEn: The Reimer–Tiemann reaction converts phenol into salicylaldehyde (2-hydroxybenzaldehyde, $\text{C}_7\text{H}_6\text{O}_2$). Molecular weight $= 7(12) + 6(1) + 2(16) = 122\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The total number of stereoisomers possible for 2,3-dibromobutane is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: 2,3-Dibromobutane has $2$ identically substituted stereocenters, yielding $3$ stereoisomers: the enantiomeric pair $(2R,3R)/(2S,3S)$ and one achiral *meso* isomer $(2R,3S)$.

questions.questionTextEn: Assuming complete dissociation of both protons, the $\text{pH}$ of a $0.0050\text{ M}$ aqueous $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution at $25\,^\circ\text{C}$ is _______. *(round off to one decimal place)*
questions.explanationEn: Complete dissociation yields $[\text{H}^+] = 2 \times 0.0050 = 0.010\text{ M} = 10^{-2}\text{ M}$, so $\text{pH} = -\log_{10}(10^{-2}) = 2.0$.

questions.questionTextEn: In the cyclic silicate anion $[\text{Si}_6\text{O}_{18}]^{12-}$ (present in beryl), the number of oxygen atoms shared per $\text{SiO}_4$ tetrahedron is _______.
questions.explanationEn: In any cyclic silicate $[\text{Si}_n\text{O}_{3n}]^{2n-}$, each $\text{SiO}_4$ tetrahedron shares exactly $2$ corner oxygen atoms with its two adjacent ring neighbors.

questions.questionTextEn: The maximum number of orbitals possible in an $f$-subshell ($l = 3$) is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: For azimuthal quantum number $l = 3$, the magnetic quantum number $m_l$ takes $2l + 1 = 2(3) + 1 = 7$ integer values ($-3, -2, -1, 0, +1, +2, +3$), corresponding to $7$ orbitals.

questions.questionTextEn: The rate constant for a first-order thermal decomposition at $400\text{ K}$ is $3.465 \times 10^{-3}\text{ s}^{-1}$. The half-life of the reaction is _______ $\text{s}$. *(round off to the nearest integer)*
questions.explanationEn: For a first-order reaction, $t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{k} = \frac{0.69315}{3.465 \times 10^{-3}} = 200.04\text{ s} \approx 200\text{ s}$.

questions.questionTextEn: The total number of geometrical stereoisomers possible for hexa-2,4-diene ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CH–CH}=\text{CHCH}_3$) is _______. *(answer in integer)*
questions.explanationEn: Because hexa-2,4-diene is symmetrically substituted at both ends, $(2E,4Z)$ and $(2Z,4E)$ are identical. The $3$ distinct geometrical isomers are $(2E,4E)$, $(2Z,4Z)$, and $(2E,4Z)$.

questions.questionTextEn: In the thorium radioactive decay series $^{232}_{90}\text{Th} \longrightarrow {}^{208}_{82}\text{Pb}$, the total number of $\alpha$-particles emitted is _______.
questions.explanationEn:
Each $\alpha$-particle ($^4_2\text{He}$) lowers the mass number $A$ by $4$, while $\beta$ emissions do not change $A$.
Hence, $n_\alpha = \frac{232 - 208}{4} = \frac{24}{4} = 6$.

questions.questionTextEn: Ignoring pairing energy, the magnitude of the crystal field stabilization energy (in units of $\Delta_o$) of low-spin $[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-}$ is _______. *(round off to one decimal place)*
questions.explanationEn:
$\text{Fe}^{2+}$ is $3d^6$; with strong-field $\text{CN}^-$ it adopts the low-spin configuration $t_{2g}^6 e_g^0$.
$\text{CFSE} = 6(-0.4\Delta_o) = -2.4\Delta_o$, so the magnitude is $2.4\Delta_o$.

questions.questionTextEn: Chloroacetic acid has $\text{p}K_a = 2.86$ and acetic acid has $\text{p}K_a = 4.76$ in water at $298\text{ K}$. The ratio of their acid dissociation constants, $K_a(\text{ClCH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}) / K_a(\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H})$, is _______. *(round off to the nearest integer)*

The solubility product of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ is $K_{sp} = 1.0 \times 10^{-11}$ at $25\,^\circ\text{C}$. The minimum $\text{pH}$ at which $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ just begins to precipitate from a $0.010\text{ M}$ aqueous $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ solution is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn: Precipitation begins when $[\text{Mg}^{2+}][\text{OH}^-]^2 = K_{sp} \implies [\text{OH}^-]^2 = \frac{1.0 \times 10^{-11}}{0.010} = 1.0 \times 10^{-9} \implies [\text{OH}^-] = 10^{-4.5}\text{ M}$. Thus $\text{pOH} = 4.50$ and $\text{pH} = 14.00 - 4.50 = 9.50$.

questions.questionTextEn:
For carbon monoxide with rotational constant $B = 1.93\text{ cm}^{-1}$ at $T = 300\text{ K}$, the rotational quantum number $J_{\max}$ of the most populated rotational level is _______. *(round off to the nearest integer)*
[Given: $k_B = 1.3806 \times 10^{-23}\text{ J K}^{-1}$, $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}$, $c = 3.0 \times 10^8\text{ m s}^{-1}$]
questions.explanationEn: Using $J_{\max} = \sqrt{\frac{k_B T}{2hcB}} - \frac{1}{2}$ with $B = 193\text{ m}^{-1}$: $\frac{k_B T}{2hcB} = \frac{1.3806\times 10^{-23} \times 300}{2 \times 6.626\times 10^{-34} \times 3.0\times 10^8 \times 193} = 53.97$. Thus $J_{\max} = \sqrt{53.97} - 0.5 = 7.35 - 0.5 = 6.85 \approx 7$.

questions.questionTextEn:
Styrene ($\text{C}_8\text{H}_8$) is epoxidized with $m$-CPBA to form styrene oxide, which is then ring-opened with $\text{NaOMe}$ in methanol (followed by neutralization) to give 2-methoxy-1-phenylethanol as the major product. The molecular weight of this final product is _______ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$. *(answer in integer)*
[Given: atomic weights $\text{H} = 1$, $\text{C} = 12$, $\text{O} = 16$]
questions.explanationEn: Styrene oxide ($\text{C}_8\text{H}_8\text{O}$) undergoes base-catalyzed $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ ring opening by $\text{MeO}^-$ at the less hindered terminal carbon to yield 2-methoxy-1-phenylethanol ($\text{PhCH(OH)CH}_2\text{OMe}$, $\text{C}_9\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_2$). Molecular weight $= 9(12) + 12(1) + 2(16) = \mathbf{152}\text{ g mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: Solvolysis of optically pure $(R)$-2-bromooctane in aqueous ethanol yields 2-octanol with $70\%$ inversion and $30\%$ retention of configuration. Given that optically pure $(S)$-2-octanol has a specific rotation $[\alpha]_D = +10.0^\circ$, the specific rotation of the isolated 2-octanol product is _______ $^\circ$. *(round off to one decimal place)*
questions.explanationEn:
Inversion of $(R)$-2-bromooctane gives $(S)$-2-octanol ($70\%$), while retention gives $(R)$-2-octanol ($30\%$). Thus, the enantiomeric excess of $(S)$-2-octanol is $70\% - 30\% = 40\%$ ($0.40$).
Observed specific rotation $= 0.40 \times (+10.0^\circ) = \mathbf{+4.0}^\circ$.

questions.questionTextEn: A two-electron galvanic cell has $E^\circ = 1.10\text{ V}$ at $298\text{ K}$ and $\left(\frac{\partial E^\circ}{\partial T}\right)_P = -5.0 \times 10^{-4}\text{ V K}^{-1}$. Taking $F = 96500\text{ C mol}^{-1}$, the standard enthalpy change $\Delta H^\circ$ for the cell reaction is _______ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. *(round off to one decimal place)*
questions.explanationEn: $\Delta H^\circ = -nF\left[E^\circ - T\left(\frac{\partial E^\circ}{\partial T}\right)_P\right] = -2(96500)[1.10 - 298(-5.0 \times 10^{-4})] = -193000(1.249) = -241057\text{ J mol}^{-1} = -241.06\text{ kJ mol}^{-1} \approx -241.1\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.questionTextEn: An ancient wooden artifact exhibits a $^{14}\text{C}$ specific activity of $10.0\text{ dpm g}^{-1}$, whereas freshly cut wood exhibits $15.0\text{ dpm g}^{-1}$. Given the half-life of $^{14}\text{C}$ as $5730\text{ years}$, the age of the artifact is _______ $\text{years}$. *(round off to the nearest integer)*
questions.explanationEn:
By first-order radioactive decay:
$t = \frac{t_{1/2}}{\ln 2}\ln\left(\frac{A_0}{A}\right) = \frac{5730}{0.693147}\ln\left(\frac{15.0}{10.0}\right) = 8266.65 \times 0.405465 = 3351.8\text{ years} \approx 3352\text{ years}$.

questions.questionTextEn: L-Lysine has the following ionizable groups: $\alpha$-carboxyl ($\text{p}K_{a1} = 2.18$), $\alpha$-ammonium ($\text{p}K_{a2} = 8.95$), and $\varepsilon$-ammonium side chain ($\text{p}K_{aR} = 10.53$). The isoelectric point ($\text{p}I$) of L-lysine is _______. *(round off to two decimal places)*
questions.explanationEn:
L-Lysine is a basic amino acid; its electrically neutral zwitterionic form predominates between the deprotonation of the $\alpha$-ammonium group ($\text{p}K_{a2} = 8.95$) and the side-chain $\varepsilon$-ammonium group ($\text{p}K_{aR} = 10.53$):
$\text{p}I = \frac{8.95 + 10.53}{2} = \mathbf{9.74}$.

questions.questionTextEn: According to the $18$-electron rule, the total number of $\text{Ir}-\text{Ir}$ single bonds in the tetrahedral metal carbonyl cluster $\text{Ir}_4(\text{CO})_{12}$ is _______.
questions.explanationEn:
Total valence electrons (TVE) $= 4(9) + 12(2) = 36 + 24 = 60\text{ e}^-$.
Number of $\text{M}-\text{M}$ bonds $= \frac{18(4) - 60}{2} = \frac{72 - 60}{2} = 6$ (corresponding to the $6$ edges of a tetrahedron).

questions.questionTextEn:
Using the Born–Landé equation, calculate the magnitude of the lattice energy $|U_0|$ (in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) of $\text{KCl}$ (rock-salt structure).

[Given: Madelung constant $A = 1.748$; equilibrium interionic distance $r_0 = 314\text{ pm}$; Born exponent $n = 9$; $\dfrac{N_A e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} = 1.389 \times 10^5\text{ kJ pm mol}^{-1}$]
*(round off to one decimal place)*
questions.explanationEn:
By the Born–Landé equation:
$|U_0| = \left(\frac{N_A e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\right) \frac{A |z_+ z_-|}{r_0}\left(1 - \frac{1}{n}\right) = (1.389 \times 10^5) \times \frac{1.748 \times 1}{314} \times \left(1 - \frac{1}{9}\right)$.
$|U_0| = 773.24 \times \frac{8}{9} = 687.3\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
